faq.q: What is the origin of Shihab?
faq.a: Shihab is associated with Arabic. Shihab is Arabic شِهَاب (Shihāb), meaning 'shooting star, meteor'.
Yes — the underlying form شِهَاب is Arabic.
Shihab can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shihab should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ش ه ب occurs in Quranic vocabulary for a shooting star, but Shihāb is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Shihab mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Shihab is rendered شهاب and carries the sense شهاب، شهاب‌سنگ.
A romanized syllable approximation is shi-hab. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Shihab, shihab. Script forms are شهاب, شِهَاب, شہاب, शिहाब.

faq.q: Is Shihab a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
